name: Capitoline Museums
places: Palazzo dei Conservatori courtyard, Capitoline Museums
description: Some of the world’s oldest public museums, in the palaces around Michelangelo’s square on the Capitoline Hill, with the bronze she-wolf.

name: St Peter’s Basilica
places: Chair of St Peter, St Peter’s Basilica
description: The Pope’s basilica and the colonnaded square in front. Inside are Michelangelo’s Pietà, Bernini’s bronze canopy and the Chair of St Peter.

name: Sistine Chapel
description: The papal chapel at the end of the Vatican Museums route, with Michelangelo’s ceiling and Last Judgement. Popes are elected here.

name: Vatican Museums
description: The popes’ art collections, spread through the Vatican palaces: ancient sculpture, Etruscan finds, the Raphael Rooms and a picture gallery.

name: Borghese Gallery
description: A 17th-century villa in the Borghese park holding sculptures by Bernini and paintings by Caravaggio. Entry is by timed booking only.

name: Colosseum
description: The amphitheatre finished in 80 AD, where gladiators fought in front of crowds of around 50,000.

name: Trevi Fountain
description: The largest baroque fountain in Rome, finished in 1762. Tradition says a coin thrown over your shoulder means you will come back.

name: Roman Forum
places: Temple of Antoninus and Faustina, Roman Forum
Arch of Septimius Severus, Roman Forum
description: The ruins of ancient Rome’s political and religious centre: temples, triumphal arches and the early frescoed church of Santa Maria Antiqua.

name: Castel Sant’Angelo
description: Hadrian’s mausoleum by the Tiber, later a papal fortress and prison. It is now a museum, with views from the terrace at the top.

name: Ponte Sant’Angelo
description: A Roman footbridge across the Tiber, built by Hadrian to reach his tomb, lined with ten baroque angels designed by Bernini.

name: Pantheon
description: A Roman temple from around 125 AD, now a church, with a huge unreinforced concrete dome open to the sky at the top.

name: Arch of Constantine
description: A triumphal arch beside the Colosseum, put up in 315 AD for the emperor Constantine, partly decorated with carvings taken from older monuments.

name: Largo di Torre Argentina
description: A sunken square of temple ruins next to the spot where Julius Caesar was killed. A cat shelter operates on the site.

name: Piazza Navona
places: Fountain of the Moor, Piazza Navona
description: A long baroque square on the outline of an ancient stadium, with three fountains, including Bernini’s Fountain of the Four Rivers.

name: Testaccio Market
description: A covered food market in the Testaccio neighbourhood, with produce stalls and counters selling Roman street food.

name: San Luigi dei Francesi
description: The church of the French community near Piazza Navona, with three Caravaggio paintings of the life of St Matthew in a side chapel.

name: Acqua Paola Fountain
description: A large early-1600s fountain on the Janiculum hill, built like a triumphal arch, with views across the city.

name: Santa Maria Maggiore
description: One of Rome’s four major papal basilicas, with fifth-century mosaics and a gilded coffered ceiling.

name: Baths of Caracalla
description: The huge brick ruins of a third-century public bath complex. Opera and concerts are staged here in summer.

name: Ara Pacis Museum
description: A glass-walled museum by the Tiber built around the Ara Pacis, a carved marble altar celebrating the peace brought by Augustus.

name: Circus Maximus
description: The site of ancient Rome’s chariot-racing stadium, now a long grassy hollow below the Palatine Hill.

name: Trajan’s Forum and Column
description: The last and largest of the imperial forums, with Trajan’s Column, carved with his wars in a spiral, and the brick market halls on the hillside.

name: San Pietro in Vincoli
description: A basilica that keeps the chains said to have bound St Peter, and Michelangelo’s statue of Moses on the tomb of Pope Julius II.

name: Santa Maria del Popolo
description: A church on Piazza del Popolo with two Caravaggio paintings, of St Paul and St Peter, and a chapel designed by Raphael.

name: National Etruscan Museum
description: A 16th-century papal villa, now the national museum of the Etruscans, the people who ruled central Italy before the Romans.

name: Palazzo Massimo
description: A branch of the National Roman Museum near Termini station, with ancient sculpture, bronzes and painted rooms from Roman villas.

name: Spanish Steps
description: A wide 18th-century stairway from Piazza di Spagna up to a church, with a boat-shaped fountain at the bottom.

name: Church of the Gesù
places: Chapel of St Ignatius, Church of the Gesù
description: The mother church of the Jesuits, with a painted ceiling that seems to open to the sky and the tomb of St Ignatius in a side chapel.

name: Sant’Andrea al Quirinale
places: Rooms of St Stanislas Kostka, Sant’Andrea al Quirinale
description: A small oval church by Bernini, with the rooms next door where the young Jesuit St Stanislas Kostka lived and died.
